Dana-Farber has launched OPTIONS-ACTIVATE, a randomized study testing whether proactive AI trial suggestions help more patients reach clinical trials.

When [MatchMiner-AI](../../matchminer-ai.qmd) detects that a patient's cancer is progressing, their oncologist receives an email with a ranked list of possible trials. The study compares this with standard MatchMiner-AI access. Its main measure is the share of new systemic treatments that are clinical trials.

It builds on an [earlier Dana-Farber randomized trial](2025-jama-progression-notifications.qmd), which found that AI could reliably spot patients likely to need a change in treatment, but that notifications alone did not raise enrollment. OPTIONS-ACTIVATE is designed around that lesson.

OPTIONS-ACTIVATE is part of ACTIVATE (AI-driven Clinical-trial Trial-Information and Viability Assessment Tool for EHRs), a research program led by Kenneth Kehl, MD, MPH, and funded by the National Cancer Institute (R37 CA295653).

- [ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07232043](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07232043)
- [Dana-Farber trial listing 25-413](https://www.dana-farber.org/clinical-trials/25-413)
